items.claim: 13:14's closing clause is claimed to recur at 14:27 and labeled 'byte-identical' while the same clause is simultaneously tagged '(skeleton tier, verified via collate.py)', a tier-naming contradiction, and no Hebrew is quoted anywhere in the row to let a reader re-collate either claim.
items.evidence: Direct byte comparison confirms the closing run מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת in oshb:Prov.13.14 is in fact byte-identical, cantillation included, to the parallel run in oshb:Prov.14.27 (יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת) -- the underlying recurrence claim holds at the BYTE tier, stronger than the row's own citation. But TIER/ORDINAL DISCIPLINE requires 'byte-identical' claims to be made only per collate truth WITH the tier named; the row's device_notes instead write 'byte-identical only to Prov.14.27 (skeleton tier, verified via collate.py)', conflating two non-equivalent tiers in one clause, and since the row quotes no Hebrew at all, that collate.py run could not have produced a checkable artifact. Sweep confirms the row's digits: the mekor-chayyim phrase (skeleton) = 4 verses book-wide (10:11, 13:14, 14:27, 16:22); the full closing clause (skeleton) = 2 verses (13:14, 14:27) -- both match the row's 'sweep: 4 total' and 'sweep: 2' digits.

items.claim: The proverb_cluster call for 13:19-13:20 never discloses that Prov.13.20 carries two ketiv/qere notes, though the brief requires any span touching the 69 K/Q notes to disclose them.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json lists Prov.13.20: 2 in the kq inventory (single witness, WLC). The staged oshb bytes show the INLINE-KETIV pattern at both sites: unpointed הלוך immediately before pointed הוֹלֵ֣ךְ, and unpointed וחכם immediately before pointed יֶחְכָּ֑ם. None of rationale, rejected_alternative, or device_notes for P06-046 mentions either note, though the row's own cluster call rests on this verse's wording. The shared plural noun for fools IS a genuine exact/word-bound match in both 13:19 and 13:20 (skeleton sweep = 17 verses book-wide for that noun, including two more within this same ch.13-14 stretch, at 14:8 -- confirming it is common, thin cohesion evidence, consistent with the row's own medium_low rating), but the undisclosed K/Q is a separate, unconditional governance violation independent of the cluster call. No Hebrew is quoted in the row.

items.claim: The homograph disclosure (13:20's companion-of verb vs. 13:21's calamity noun sharing consonants only) and the object-marker-plus-waw connector claim both verify correct, but neither is grounded by a quoted Hebrew run.
items.evidence: 13:20 carries וְרֹעֶ֖ה (root associated with 'companion of') and יֵרֽוֹעַ (from a harm-root), while 13:21 opens its B-colon with וְאֶת צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים (waw plus the object marker, exactly as claimed) and closes with רָעָ֑ה ('evil/calamity'). At the bare skeleton tier the consonants of וְרֹעֶ֖ה and רָעָ֑ה do share the string, confirming the row's homograph call is accurate rather than a genuine catchword -- correct disclosure. Substance verifies correct; the sole defect is evidentiary: no Hebrew is quoted for either the connector or the homograph claim, so a reader cannot re-collate them without independently pulling the source bytes.

items.claim: The distinction drawn between 13:22's plain tov-subject opener and 12:9's genuine tov-min comparative is correct and confirmed against the device inventory, but the row quotes no Hebrew to support it.
items.evidence: prov_device_inventory.json tov_openers lists Prov.13.22 among its 16 refs, confirming the row's premise. 12:9 opens with ט֣וֹב and carries the min-prefixed comparative וַחֲסַר later in the verse; 13:22 opens with the identical word ט֗וֹב but has no min-comparative anywhere in the verse -- the row's claim that 13:22 is a bare subject rather than a tov-min saying is byte-confirmed. No Hebrew run is quoted in the row itself to let a reader verify this without independent extraction.

items.claim: The disputed-noun crux (a 'heads/chiefs' noun vs. WEB's 'poor people' gloss) is correctly identified as a genuine gap between the consonants and the English rendering, but the row never quotes the noun in Hebrew to show the letter that makes the crux real.
items.evidence: The staged oshb bytes for Prov.13.23 read נִ֣יר רָאשִׁ֑ים, with the aleph present in the second word -- the 'heads/chiefs' reading, not the aleph-less 'poor' word that WEB's gloss implies. This confirms the row's claim that WEB's 'poor people' is not transparent from the bare consonants as staged: a genuine, byte-grounded lexical crux, correctly disclosed rather than resolved. But the row quotes no Hebrew, so the very letter the crux turns on is invisible to a reader checking the row without independently pulling the source bytes.

items.claim: The petuchah-as-corroboration-only framing and the chapter-close claim both verify correct and are the best-disclosed mark citation in this cluster, but the waw-adversative claim underlying the antithetic call is still asserted without a quoted Hebrew run.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json / parashah_distribution confirm Prov.13.25 carries chapter 13's only PE seg, and Prov.13.26 does not exist in the staged extract (14:1 begins the next chapter), so both the 'range's one disclosed petuchah' and 'closes chapter 13' claims check out. The device_notes correctly name the ref, tier (petuchah, single-witness) and hold it as corroboration only per governance -- the standard the rest of this cluster should meet. The verse's own וּבֶ֖טֶן confirms the claimed waw-adversative opens the B-colon, but that token is never quoted in the row.

items.claim: The imperative opener and the rare-negative-particle match with 12:3 both verify exact, and the row correctly discloses the 14:6 knowledge-noun seam-adjacency as ordinary vocabulary rather than overstating it as cohesion evidence, but again no Hebrew is quoted.
items.evidence: 14:7 opens with the imperative לֵ֣ךְ and closes with וּבַל יָ֝דַ֗עְתָּ; 12:3 independently carries בַּל יִמּֽוֹט -- the same less-common negative particle (against the book's ordinary negator) confirmed present in both verses at the skeleton tier, exactly as the row claims. 14:6 and 14:7 do share the knowledge-noun (וְדַ֖עַת in 14:6, שִׂפְתֵי דָֽעַת closing 14:7), and the row discloses this itself as 'ordinary vocabulary, not a construction run' rather than misusing it as cluster evidence -- correct restraint. Substance fully verifies; the only defect is that none of these forms is actually quoted in the row for independent re-collation.

items.claim: The proverb_cluster rationale for 14:12-13 rests on the shared 'its end' hinge-word, but omits that 14:12 is byte-identical to Prov.16.25 elsewhere in the book, where that same line stands as a fully self-contained proverb sharing no content token with either neighbor -- direct evidence that 14:12 does not need 14:13 to be complete.
items.evidence: Direct byte comparison confirms oshb:Prov.14.12 (יֵ֤שׁ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יָ֭שָׁר לִפְנֵי אִ֑ישׁ וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ דַּרְכֵי מָֽוֶת) and oshb:Prov.16.25 (יֵ֤שׁ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יָ֭שָׁר לִפְנֵי אִ֑ישׁ וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ דַּרְכֵי מָֽוֶת) are fully byte-identical, cantillation included. At 16:25's own location its neighbors -- Prov.16.24 and Prov.16.26 -- share zero content tokens with it, so the MT itself reuses this exact line as a standalone proverb with no dependent partner anywhere else in the book. This directly undercuts the row's central claim that the shared hinge-word 'is why these two verses read as a matched pair... giving it more weight than the range's thinner one-token catchword pairs' -- the same verse demonstrably works alone elsewhere. The hinge-word itself, וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ / וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ, is confirmed exact word-bound in both 14:12 and 14:13 (root sweep = 13 verses book-wide), so the observation is not fabricated, but its weight for clustering is overstated given the undisclosed duplicate. No Hebrew is quoted anywhere in the row.
